recipes.name: Chocolate Chia Seed Pudding
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon hazelnut flavor instant coffee powder

steps.text: Combine cocoa powder, brown sugar, and instant coffee powder in a bowl; stir until no lumps remain.
Fold chia seeds into mixture; stir in milk to incorporate. Let mixture sit a few minutes before stirring again. Repeat resting and stirring for about 20 minutes.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap; refrigerate 2 hours to overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Chia Seed Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This simple, tasty chocolate chia pudding recipe uses nutrient-dense chia seeds to make a healthy dessert. You can find the superfood in most markets.

review.reviewBody: I liked this and really wasn't sure what to think at first. I followed the recipe exactly except using 1 percent milk and plain instant coffee, which worked fine. I also just mixed the honey in with the milk, but I liked that it still wasn't too sweet. After taking it from the fridge, I wasn't too happy with it at first. The chia seed texture was just so odd. The seeds were a mix of a gel and crunchy texture which did not work for me. However, I decided to stick the pudding in the vitamix to whip it up. I normally use chia seeds in smoothies with no problem. It made the pudding nice and smooth at about 30 seconds on high. Chia seeds are so good for the stomach and I have not had any indigestion, today, which I normally do. I will definitely make this again, but double it to get more than 2 servings, and definitely blend it all together again when it is done chilling in the fridge. ty

My new favorite dessert. I add 1/2 teaspoon vanilla as well. Allow the mixture to sit at room temp for an hour versus 30 mins to speed up liquid absorption (the seeds swell faster at warm temps). In addition, microwave the milk for a minute to warm it up before stirring it into the dry ingredients. It better dissolves the sugar and speeds up the absorption as well. Absolutely FABULOUS dessert. Must try it!

I used this as a base and it came out fantastic --- 16 ounces unsweetened almond cocount milk + 1/2 cup chia seeds , soak overnight. Next day, add 4 packets of Stevia, 1 tsp. vanilla, 1 scoop protein powder. Mix in food processor. Divide in bell jars. Top with raspberries and chopped nuts.

I liked it. Added plant based half and half, just a splash. Oat milk from the shelf, not refrigerated( twice as much sugar). Cinnamon, Peanut butter, mashed banana. Added blue berries and mixed unsalted nuts. Have to let it sit alittle longer,overnight is perferred, it has more liquid than container calls for . But enjoyed it. I make the choc. version for my husband but not for me. I have t2 diabetes, a sprinkle of sugar free creamer is a game changer. I omit brown sugar, and add only a small amount of honey. But my blood sugar did go way up. So I had to walk about 15 mins. to get it down.

I didn’t follow recipe fully as I used unsweetened almond milk vs milk, Monk fruit sweetener vs brown sugar and plain instant coffee. I didn’t mind the texture but my hubby who hates tapioca pudding thought the texture resembles that so I used immersion blender to smooth it out for him. He has a real sweet tooth and as we are trying really hard to eat healthier I didn’t hold up much hope that he would enjoy this and he did!

This was sooooo good! Perfect afternoon sweet treat. As another reviewer suggested I used unsweetened almond milk and splenda brown sugar. I had a packet of tasters choice instant hazelnut coffee on hand, so I threw that in and I think that enhanced the chocolate flavor. I also blended the mixture in my magic bullet as suggested by another reviewer. I actually made the mixture in the magic bullet cup so when it was done in the frig I just screwed on the blades and blended. I did add a few chopped walnuts - reminded me of fudge! Very tasty - will definitely make again.

Replaced with coconut sugar, cut the sugar, added vanilla extract and a little salt. You always need a little salt to bring out the chocolate flavor. Also I ground up cacao nibs and add them. I use raw organic cacao powder Oat milk. I quadruple this recipe, it's too little. This is a low calorie treat. Very filling, great for a snack.

I made it with a few adjustments. I'm not a fan of the texture of chia seeds so I blended it with the cocoa powder. I used maple syrup instead of brown sugar and added this along with vanilla essence and milk to the dry ingredients and blended further which helped it to thicken up. I can't wait to have this for breakfast tomorrow with some sliced strawberries

I'm love this recipe. I tripeled the recipe and add 1/3 cup honey before storing as well as drizzle honey just before serving. I also used Coconut Milk in place of regular milk which makes it creamier. It's addicting.

I loved it, definitely deserves 5 stars. It satisfied my chocolate craving. The only problem is, that when I take it out the milk has separated from the chia seeds and while the bottom layer consists of milk, the top only has chia seeds. That is easily fixed though, I just have to mix it a little. Definitely recommend, despite the issue. I use organic blue agave instead of honey because I don’t like the taste of honey, and it tasted even better in my opinion. I think the chia pudding definitely is way better with the sweetness added to it. I also add a dash of vanilla for flavor. I didn’t add any instant coffee because I don’t like coffee. Overall, statistics both my sweet tooth and chocolate craving.
Good recipe. I added 1/4 cup plain yogurt for added protein.

I’m usually a picky eater & I’ll make chia pudding just to not end up liking it. This one tastes actually GOOD. i think the instant coffee made it! also 1 serving of CHIA SEEDS is 1-2tbsp per day so id recommend eating half of this at a time. i used swerve brown sugar & unsweetened vanilla almond milk.
Turned out great! I used cane sugar instead of brown and it came out very nicely. I added frozen raspberries to mine.
It was great! I agree with the warm milk using, and it was a family favorite! I recommend adding banana, then peanut butter (liquified) on top. You could also use strawberries. Then it is perfect!

I love this. Really helped my chocolate cravings! The texture is like tapioca to me. Mine did solidify like a jello, but it was still delicious. Probably needs more than a cup of milk. Ok, so I added a half cup of chia instead of a quarter. Made it again with Stevia, honey, skim milk, vanilla and the seeds and a tbsp of instant regular coffee bc that's what I had. Can't wait to taste!

I added a pinch of salt and dash of vanilla as some recommended and they enhanced the flavor. I didn't use the dried coffee. I did choose to use 3/4 cup whole milk and 1/4 cup half & half and it was decadent. This is an easy and delicious treat.
I loved it! Used coconut milk instead of regular milk.

I’ve made this a few times now. It’s always good. I’ve omitted the instant coffee & that was good. I have used oat milk & that was good. With or without the honey drizzle, a little different flavor but still yummy. A healthy alternative for me as a chocoholic! Thank you!
My husband likes this even better than traditional chocolate pudding.

I changed the recipe a bit-used almond milk and real maple syrup since I’m plant based and have cut out processed sugar.
I’d definitely make this again with some changes.
I’d use coconut milk and blend in my Nutri bullet like I read in a review after making it.
It works for my sweet tooth craving.
